div.div: هَجٍ and هَجْ, (S, K,) like as one says نَخٍ and بَخْ, (S,) or هِجِى. as related by Lh, (L,) and هَجا (K,) or هَجٍ هَجٍ and هَجْ هجْ and ??. (Az,) Cries by which one chides a dog. (S, K,) and a lion, and a wolf, &c., to quiet him: (Az:) and sometimes one says هَجَا هَجَا (ISd,) and, if he please, هَجا, once, (Az) to chide camels (ISd, Az) and هَجْ, or هَج at the end of a verse is a cry by which a she-camel is chidden. (L.) For هَجْ هَجْ, one also says جَهْ جَهْ, by transposition. (L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
